questions.q: In the official order of execution, do validation rules run before or after before-triggers?
options: Validation rules always run first, before any trigger
Validation rules run after before-triggers, so they see any changes a before-trigger made
Validation rules and triggers never interact
Validation rules only run after the record is committed
questions.explain: Before-triggers run, then validation runs again including custom validation rules, so a before-trigger can normalize a value before the rule evaluates it.

questions.q: What happens if a duplicate rule blocks a record during the save procedure?
options: The record saves anyway with a warning
Only the validation rules are skipped, everything else still runs
The record isn't saved, and no further steps like after triggers or workflow rules run
The record is saved but marked inactive
questions.explain: A duplicate rule set to block stops the save procedure entirely at that point; after triggers and workflow never get a chance to run.

questions.q: When a workflow rule performs a field update, what gets re-run?
options: Nothing is re-run; the field simply changes silently
The entire order of execution restarts from step 1, including duplicate rules
The record updates again, system validation runs again, and before/after update triggers run one more time, but not validation rules or duplicate rules
Only Process Builder and flows re-run
questions.explain: A workflow field update causes a partial re-run: the update, system validation, and triggers fire once more, but custom validation rules and duplicate rules are not run again.

questions.q: In what order do Process Builder processes and flows launched by workflow rules execute relative to each other?
options: Process Builder always runs before any workflow-launched flow
Alphabetically by process name
In no guaranteed order relative to each other
In the order they were created
questions.explain: Salesforce documents these as running in no guaranteed order relative to each other, which is part of why record-triggered flows (with controllable ordering) are preferred for new automation.

questions.q: When does post-commit logic, like sending email or running queueable Apex jobs, actually execute?
options: Before the record is saved to the database
Immediately after before-triggers run
Only after all DML operations have been committed to the database
During duplicate rule evaluation
questions.explain: Post-commit logic is the very last phase, running only after everything else in the save procedure has committed.
